audit.whatIsWrong: Five rows disagree with the already-audited mirror and the packet chart. Levels 2 and 3 read Cho'Gath here while the mirror sets both to Sylas; Level 6 reads Skill while the mirror sets it to Cho'Gath; First item and Two+ items read Cho'Gath while the mirror sets both to Skill.
audit.why: The mirror is the paid-for authority and mirror-fix.js overwrites disagreements. Levels 2-3 are genuinely Sylas's — Cho'Gath has no mobility and his pre-tank stats do not survive a full rotation — and the later rows even out rather than belonging to him.
audit.corrected: Levels 2 and 3 read Sylas at 7/10, Level 6 reads Cho'Gath at 3/10, First item and Two+ items read Skill. Proposed as one group with phases[4].why rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entire entry is built on 'commit when Rupture is down' and never says how long that is.
audit.why: Rupture is a flat 6s cooldown at every rank — the window is a few seconds, not a lane phase, and a player told to wait for it without the number will wait for something that never really arrives. Feral Scream is 9-11s, Feast is 80/70/60s against your Hijack at 80/55/30s.
audit.corrected: Rupture's 6s written into the cooldown breakdown, whys[3] and mid; Feral Scream's 9-11s and the Feast-versus-Hijack comparison added to mid and spikes[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: Three errors. (a) Vorpal Spikes is labelled '(passive)' in the early text and wants.foe[1]; it is his E, and his passive is Carnivore, which restores health and mana on kills. (b) wants.foe[1] says he stacks HP from 'Vorpal Spikes (passive)' — HP growth comes from Feast kills only. (c) Sylas's E is called a stun in whys[1], early and wants.you[0]; Abscond/Abduct has no CC in Riot's text or the kit flags, the recast pulls him to the target.
audit.why: Vorpal Spikes on his E means it is on an 8-4s cooldown attached to his attacks, not a free permanent aura, and Carnivore is why he never has to leave lane. A stun Sylas does not have changes how the player commits to every all-in.
audit.corrected: Vorpal Spikes named as his E and Carnivore as the passive; HP stacking attributed to Feast alone; the chain restated as a pull.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere says that resistances do not answer Feast, and the itemisation line offers Mercs, Steelcaps and Abyssal Mask as though they help.
audit.why: Feast is true damage — armour and MR are the wrong purchase against it. Health and staying above its threshold are the answer.
audit.corrected: Stated in whys[6] and the late text: resistances do nothing against Feast, so buy health and respect the threshold instead.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] says a stolen Feast 'scales with AP and YOUR stacks', and the late text implies a 700 AP Sylas one-shots with it.
audit.why: Riot's text gives Feast a high amount of true damage with health growth on a kill; no AP ratio is stated. Promising an AP-scaling execute is a claim the kit does not support.
audit.corrected: Restated as a flat true-damage execute that is strong because it ignores resistances and denies him the stack, not because it scales with your AP.

edits.before: Hijack online — you now own a copy of Cho'Gath's ultimate. The all-in math and every 2v2 swing your way.
edits.after: He gets Feast the same level you get Hijack — 60-80s of true-damage execute threat you cannot itemise around.

edits.before: - Cho'Gath Rupture (Knockup): matchup-defining — Telegraphed knockup — sidestep it and he has no engage at all. Check it before every step-up. - E1 shield is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Cho'Gath Rupture: matchup-defining — a telegraphed knockup on a flat 6s, so the gap is short; sidestep it and he has no engage. - Feral Scream silences your whole rotation on 9-11s. - Feast is true damage; resistances do nothing.

edits.before: E online: E1 shield absorbs his poke, E2 chain stuns him in place, and W heals back the HP cost — Cho'Gath has no mobility to escape the sequence once it lands.
edits.after: E online: E1 closes the gap, the E2 recast pulls you onto him, and W heals back the HP cost — Cho'Gath has no mobility at all to escape the sequence once it starts.

edits.before: Rupture's longer range and his growing tank stats mean every mis-timed approach is punished — trade only when his Q is visibly down or you'll be knocked up mid-E and left exposed.
edits.after: Rupture's 950 range and flat 6s cooldown mean the safe gap is seconds, not a lane phase — step in the moment it lands and misses, or you get knocked up mid-E and left exposed.

edits.before: Cho'Gath's stacked HP, Rupture lockdown, and Feral Scream silence outlast your W sustain in a straight 1v1 — use Hijack as an execute tool on carries in teamfights, not as a tank-dueling tool.
edits.after: Stacked HP, Rupture lockdown and a 9-11s silence outlast your W sustain in a straight 1v1, and Feast's true damage ignores whatever resistances you bought — use Hijack on their carries, not on him.

edits.before: Hijacking Feast is a double win: you gain a true-damage execute that scales with AP and YOUR stacks, and Cho'Gath loses his primary kill-and-grow threat for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Hijacking Feast is a double win: you gain a true-damage execute no resistance stops, and Cho'Gath cannot grow while his own 80s copy sits on cooldown behind your 80s one.

edits.before: Sidestep Rupture (Q knockup) before committing E — a grounded E2 hook stuns him and opens the W heal trade on your terms
edits.after: Sidestep Rupture, then commit E inside its 6s gap — the E2 pull lands you on a champion with no dash to answer it

edits.before: Stack Feast kills and Vorpal Spikes (passive) HP to outscale your W sustain and become unkillable in extended fights
edits.after: Stack Feast kills for permanent health and let Carnivore refill him off the wave so he never has to leave lane

edits.before: Level 1 is genuinely even — you have Q slow or W available but no hook, and Cho'Gath can poke with Vorpal Spikes (passive) autos and farm safely. Don't step into melee range to trade; last-hit from Q range and read his Rupture animation. The moment Rupture is on cooldown, you can step up freely — without it he has zero engage. At level 2, E comes online and the dynamic shifts: dash in with E1 to absorb a hit on the shield, then E2 chain onto him for the stun, Q slow, W heal. His silence (W) is the only interrupt — bait it or time your W cast before he gets it off. By level 3 you have the full rotation and his pre-tank stats can't survive a full chain without backing off.
edits.after: Level 1 is genuinely even — you have Q slow or W available but no hook, and Cho'Gath pokes with Vorpal Spikes on his autos while Carnivore refills him off every minion. Don't step into melee range to trade; last-hit from Q range and read his Rupture animation. The moment Rupture misses you have about six seconds — without it he has zero engage. At level 2, E comes online and the dynamic shifts: dash in with E1, recast to pull yourself onto him, Q slow, W heal. Feral Scream is his only interrupt on 11s — bait it or get your W off before he does. By level 3 your full rotation beats his pre-tank stats outright.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are skill-dependent because Cho'Gath's Rupture is now more dangerous to respect — if he lands it during your E approach you lose your hook window entirely and stand in the open as a melee mage. Play the clock: track Rupture's cooldown visually, and only commit your E when it is spent or on the last half-second of cast. The W heal and passive burst autos let you win extended trades when you get in cleanly, but don't overstay if Feral Scream (W silence) hits mid-chain. At level 6 the lane swings: Hijack steals Feast and you now have a true-damage execute while Cho'Gath loses his primary threat for its full cooldown — look for the all-in immediately before he backs or buys Tank Mythic items.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are skill-dependent because Rupture is now genuinely punishing — land it on your E approach and you lose the window entirely, standing in the open as a melee mage. Play the clock: it is a flat 6s, so commit the instant it lands and misses, not before. The W heal and Petricite autos win the extended trade when you get in cleanly, but do not overstay into Feral Scream's 9-11s silence. At 6 the lane tightens rather than swings: you get Feast on 80s and so does he, and his version grows him permanently — take the all-in while his is spent, and never while yours is. Ping your jungler for that window: he has no dash, so any second body on him turns the pull into a kill rather than a trade.

edits.before: At two or more items Cho'Gath's raw HP wall starts to outpace your W sustain, and his Rupture plus silence make approaching him alone a coinflip. You remain relevant by stealing Feast and using it on priority targets in teamfights — a 700+ AP Sylas casting Feast on a fed carry is often a one-shot — but you cannot 1v1 a fully-stacked Cho'Gath without jungle help or a hard lead. Focus on flanking the backline with your stolen R, not on re-engaging the tank who has been eating all game.
edits.after: At two or more items Cho'Gath's raw HP wall starts to outpace your W sustain, and Rupture plus the silence make approaching him alone a coinflip. You remain relevant by stealing Feast for priority targets in teamfights — true damage means no resistance on their carry matters — but you cannot 1v1 a fully-stacked Cho'Gath without jungle help or a hard lead. Buy health rather than MR against him, and flank the backline with the stolen R instead of re-engaging the thing that has been eating all game.

notes: Vorpal Spikes was labelled his passive in two places; it is his E, and Carnivore is the passive that keeps him in lane. Rupture's flat 6s cooldown is the number the whole entry needed — 'wait for Rupture to be down' without it reads as a lane-phase window when it is a few seconds. I removed the Sylas E stun claims here even though the chogath mirror deliberately abstained on them: the camille and akshan mirrors both confirm Abscond/Abduct has no CC, and Riot's text agrees, so leaving them would keep this entry inconsistent with the rest of the champion. The level-6 flip to Cho'Gath follows the mirror, but whys[4] still argues the Hijack window is decisive there — the two read as tension rather than contradiction, and I left whys[4] alone rather than invent a reason it is his level.
